literal: That night Rui was asleep when he saw a man about fifteen chi tall, with arms more than ten chi long, standing in the doorway facing the bed; the man pressed Rui with his arm for a long while, then vanished.
idiomatic: That night Rui lay asleep when he saw a figure some fifteen chi tall, arms more than ten chi long, blocking the doorway and leaning over the bed. The arm pressed down on him a long while — then the apparition was gone.

literal: Rui felt it deeply ill-omened; he rose at once and sighed alone: "A great man's fate has come to this in a single morning!
idiomatic: The omen filled Rui with dread. He sat up alone and sighed: "A great man's fate — to reach this in a single morning!

literal: " Fearing the empress dowager would kill him, at dawn he wished to enter court; his wife and children all remonstrated and stopped him.
idiomatic: " Fearing the empress dowager meant to kill him, at dawn he would go to court; wife and children all pleaded with him to stay.

literal: Rui said: "Since ancient times loyal ministers have never spared their own lives; the altars weigh heavier than I — I ought to die in their service. How could I let one woman overturn the ancestral temple?
idiomatic: Rui said, "Loyal ministers since antiquity have never counted their lives; the realm matters more than I — I should die for it. How can I let one woman overturn the altars?"

literal: Besides, what sort of wretch is He Shikai, to run rampant like this? I would rather die serving the late emperor than live to see the court thrown into turmoil.
idiomatic: And what is He Shikai but a base upstart, strutting as he pleases? I would rather die serving the late emperor than watch the court come apart.

literal: " Reaching the palace gate, someone again said: "I beg Your Highness not to enter — I fear sudden danger.
idiomatic: " At the palace gate another voice said, "Do not go in, Highness — there may be treachery.

literal: " Rui said: "Above I owe Heaven; even in death I have no regret.
idiomatic: " Rui said, "I owe Heaven; if I die, I die without regret.

literal: " He entered and saw the empress dowager; she again spoke as before, but Rui held all the more firmly.
idiomatic: " He went in to the empress dowager; she argued as before, but Rui would not yield.

literal: Leaving he reached the Eternal Lane, met soldiers, was seized, and sent to Hualin Garden; at the Sparrow-Departure Buddhist cloister Liu Taozhi strangled and killed him. He was thirty-six.
idiomatic: Leaving the palace he reached Eternal Lane, was seized by soldiers, and sent to Hualin Garden. At Sparrow-Departure Cloister Liu Taozhi strangled him. He was thirty-six.

literal: Heavy fog lasted three days; court and countryside mourned the injustice.
idiomatic: Thick fog shrouded the land for three days; court and countryside grieved the injustice.

literal: A year later an edict permitted burial with princely rites; in the end no posthumous title was granted.
idiomatic: A year later an edict allowed princely burial — but no posthumous name was ever granted.

literal: His son Zheng inherited the succession.
idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

literal: He served in succession as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and honorary equal to the three ducal ministers.

literal: Fond of learning and upright in conduct, in youth he fell from a horse while hunting, injuring his waist and legs; he never walked again and died at Chang'an.
idiomatic: He loved learning and kept his conduct straight. As a youth he fell from his horse on a hunt and injured waist and legs; he never walked again and died at Chang'an.

literal: Chen's younger half-brother Huibao died young; in the first year of Yuanxiang he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Military Governor of Four Provinces, Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: Chen's younger half-brother Huibao died young; in the first year of Yuanxiang he was posthumously made palace attendant, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, and military governor of four provinces and governor of Qing Province.

literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was again posthumously made Military Governor of Ten Provinces, enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, posthumous name Wengong; the tenth son of Prince of Qinghe Yue, Jingwen, was made heir.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tiantong he was again posthumously made military governor of ten provinces and enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, posthumous name Wengong; Gao Yue's tenth son Jingwen was made his heir.

literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue, courtesy name Honglüe, was a younger cousin of the High Ancestor on the father's side.
idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue, courtesy name Honglüe, was a younger cousin of Gao Huan.

literal: His father Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor by Wei and given posthumous name Duke Xiaoxuan.
idiomatic: His father Gao Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously made grand preceptor by Wei and given the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.

literal: Yue in youth was orphaned and poor; no one yet knew him. Grown, he was honest and upright, of lofty bearing, deep and reserved, with great capacity.
idiomatic: Yue was orphaned and poor in youth; no one yet marked him. Grown, he was honest and upright, of striking bearing — deep, reserved, and possessed of great capacity.

literal: At first Yue's family lived at Luoyang; whenever the High Ancestor came to Luoyang on mission he always lodged at Yue's house.
idiomatic: At first Yue's household was at Luoyang; whenever Gao Huan came to the capital on business he always stayed at Yue's house.

literal: Yue's mother, Lady Shan, once rose at night and saw light in the High Ancestor's chamber; she stole a look — there was no lamp — and moved the High Ancestor to another room; the same sight appeared as before.
idiomatic: Yue's mother Lady Shan once rose at night and saw light in Gao Huan's room. She stole a look — no lamp burned — and moved him to another chamber; the same radiance appeared there.

literal: Marveling at the portent, she went to a diviner who cast and obtained Qian changing to Dayou; the reading said: "Auspicious. The Changes says, 'The flying dragon is in heaven — the great man creates.' Flying dragon, the fifth line — the hexagram of the great man; honor beyond words.
idiomatic: Struck by the omen, she consulted a diviner and obtained Qian changing to Dayou. The reading ran: "Auspicious. The Changes says, 'The flying dragon is in heaven — the great man creates.' The fifth line — the great man's hexagram; honor beyond words.

literal: " Lady Shan returned and reported to the High Ancestor.
idiomatic: " Lady Shan went back and told Gao Huan.

literal: Later when the High Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, Lady Shan heard and rejoiced greatly; she told Yue: "The omen of red light is now fulfilled — you should go by secret route and join him; together plot the great design.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan later raised troops at Xindu, Lady Shan heard and rejoiced. She told Yue, "The omen of red light is fulfilled — go by a secret route and join him; together you will shape the great design.

literal: " Yue thereupon went to Xindu.
idiomatic: " Yue went to Xindu.

literal: The High Ancestor saw him and was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Gao Huan saw him and was greatly pleased.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, concurrently commanding the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the east, and grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, concurrently commanding the martial guard.

literal: The High Ancestor fought the Four Hus at Hanling; the High Ancestor commanded the center, Gao Ang the left, Yue the right.
idiomatic: Gao Huan fought the Four Hus at Hanling: he himself held the center, Gao Ang the left, Yue the right.

literal: The center was routed; the enemy pressed in. Yue raised his banner and shouted, charging straight through the enemy line; the High Ancestor was thus able to wheel about, and front and rear struck together, breaking the enemy completely.
idiomatic: The center broke; the enemy pressed in. Yue raised his banner and shouted, driving straight through their line — Gao Huan could wheel about, and front and rear together smashed the foe.

literal: For merit he was made Guard General and Right Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, still commanding the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: For this he was made guard general and right grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, still commanding the martial guard.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Chariot-and-Horse General and Left Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, commanding the Left and Right Guards, enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made chariot-and-horse general and left grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon, commanding the left and right guards, enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe Commandery with two thousand households.

literal: His mother Lady Shan was enfeoffed Lady of the Commandery; a daughter was made Lady Attendant Within and entered to serve the empress.
idiomatic: His mother Lady Shan was enfeoffed lady of the commandery; a daughter was made lady attendant within and entered to serve the empress.

literal: At that time Erzhu Rong still held Bing Province; the High Ancestor was about to attack him and ordered Yue to remain guarding the capital, promoting him to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong still held Bing Province; Gao Huan meant to attack him and left Yue to guard the capital, promoting him to grand general of the flying cavalry and honorary equal to the three ducal ministers.

literal: In the second year of Tianping he was made Palace Attendant and Military Governor of Six Provinces; soon opening-establishment was added.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping he was made palace attendant and military governor of six provinces; soon opening-establishment was added.

literal: Yue recruited men of the age and made them staff; commentators held this admirable.
idiomatic: Yue recruited the worthy of the age for his staff; commentators praised it.

literal: Soon he was made director of the Palace Library, again tutor to the heir, and made Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor of Six Provinces, and Chief Rectifier of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the palace library, again tutor to the heir, bearer of the staff, military governor of six provinces, and chief rectifier of Ji Province.

literal: Shortly he was made Grand Governor of the Capital Region; all affairs of the six provinces were referred to the capital region.
idiomatic: Shortly he was made grand governor of the capital region; all six provinces' business came under the capital region.

literal: At that time the High Ancestor directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue with Palace Attendant Sun Teng and others assisted government in the capital.
idiomatic: Gao Huan then directed affairs from Jinyang; Yue with palace attendant Sun Teng and others governed at the capital.

literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he left office on his mother's death.
idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanxiang he left office to mourn his mother.

literal: Yue was utterly filial, exerting himself in tending her with full devotion; when his mother was ill he never unbelted his robe; in mourning he wasted away to the bone. The High Ancestor was deeply troubled and daily sent men to comfort him.
idiomatic: Yue was utterly filial, serving her with every devotion; when she was ill he never unbelted his robe; in mourning he wasted to skin and bone. Gao Huan was deeply troubled and sent men daily to comfort him.

literal: Soon he was recalled to his original post.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to his former post.

literal: In the second year he was additionally made Concurrent Commander of the Army.
idiomatic: In the second year he was additionally made concurrent commander of the army.

literal: At the beginning of Xinghe the Heir Apparent took overall charge of government; Yue went out as Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor, and Governor of Ji Province; palace attendant, flying-cavalry general, and opening-establishment honors remained as before.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xinghe the heir apparent took charge of government; Yue went out as bearer of the staff, military governor, and governor of Ji Province; palace attendant, flying-cavalry general, and opening-establishment honors remained.

literal: In the third year he was transferred to Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Qing Province.

literal: Yue had long held power and was feared by court and countryside alike; as governor of two provinces the people looked to the wind and trembled.
idiomatic: Yue had held power long; court and countryside alike feared him. As governor of two provinces the people looked to the wind and trembled.

literal: In the first year of Wuding he was made Governor of Jin Province and Grand Governor of the Southwest Circuit, winning praise for pacifying the frontier.
idiomatic: In the first year of Wuding he was made governor of Jin Province and grand governor of the southwest circuit, winning praise for pacifying the frontier.

literal: When Yue fell ill the High Ancestor had him return to Bing for treatment; when the illness cleared he was again ordered to his post.
idiomatic: When Yue fell ill Gao Huan had him return to Bing for treatment; when he recovered he was sent back to his post.

literal: When the High Ancestor died and Hou Jing rebelled, the Heir Apparent summoned Yue back to Bing to plan together the campaign against Jing.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan died and Hou Jing rebelled, Gao Cheng summoned Yue back to Bing to plan the campaign against Jing.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang seized the moment and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming at the head of an army at Hanshan, damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng, coordinating with Jing in pincer support.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang seized the moment and sent his Marquis of Zhenyang Ming with an army to Hanshan, damming the Si to flood Pengcheng and coordinating with Jing in pincer support.

literal: Yue commanded the armies south in punitive expedition; with the field headquarters Murong Shaozong and others he attacked Ming, routed him completely, captured Ming and his great general Hu Guisun on the field, and took tens of thousands more captive.
idiomatic: Yue led the armies south; with field headquarters Murong Shaozong and others he attacked Ming, routed him completely, captured Ming and his great general Hu Guisun on the field, and took tens of thousands more captive.

literal: Jing then massed troops at Woyang, locked in stalemate with Left Guard General Liu Feng and others.
idiomatic: Jing then massed troops at Woyang, locked in stalemate with left guard general Liu Feng and others.

literal: Yue turned his army to pursue and again defeated him; Jing fled alone on horseback.
idiomatic: Yue wheeled to pursue and defeated him again; Jing fled alone on horseback.

literal: In the sixth year, for merit he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor; the rest as before; separately enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, for merit, he was made palace attendant and grand preceptor; other offices unchanged; separately enfeoffed viscount of Xinchang.

literal: He was also made Bearer of the Staff, Grand Governor of Henan, and Grand Commander, commanding Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to attack Wang Sizheng at Changshe.
idiomatic: He was also made bearer of the staff, grand governor of Henan, and grand commander, leading Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others against Wang Sizheng at Changshe.

literal: Sizheng held the city and defended; Yue and the rest diverted the Wei River to flood it.
idiomatic: Sizheng held the city; Yue and the rest diverted the Wei River to flood it.

literal: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng; troops from west of the Pass came to aid Sizheng; Yue defended within and without with shrewd calculation.
idiomatic: Shaozong and Liu Feng were captured by Sizheng; troops from west of the Pass came to aid him; Yue defended within and without with shrewd calculation.

literal: The city was not submerged by more than three boards' thickness.
idiomatic: Only three boards' thickness of wall stood above the flood.

literal: The Heir Apparent came in person; within days beneath the walls Sizheng and the rest were captured.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng came in person; within days beneath the walls Sizheng and the rest were captured.

literal: For merit he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Zhending; the Heir Apparent claimed the credit for himself, so rewards were not fully granted.
idiomatic: For merit he was separately enfeoffed baron of Zhending; Gao Cheng claimed the credit, so rewards were not fully granted.

literal: When the Heir Apparent died the Manifest Ancestor went out to administer Jinyang and ordered Yue to remain at his original post while additionally serving as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, guarding the capital.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng died Gao Yang went out to administer Jinyang and left Yue at his original post while additionally serving as left vice minister of the Masters of Writing, guarding the capital.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery; soon made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, Opener with Honors Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Preceptor of the Imperial Clan, and Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to Prince of Qinghe Commandery; soon made bearer of the staff, grand general of the flying cavalry, opener with honors equal to the three ducal ministers, preceptor of the imperial clan, and governor of Si Province.

literal: In the fifth year Grand Preceptor was added.
idiomatic: In the fifth year grand preceptor was added.

literal: Xiao Yi of Liang, pressed by Zhou armies, sent envoys reporting emergency and requesting aid.
idiomatic: Xiao Yi of Liang, pressed by Zhou armies, sent envoys begging aid.

literal: In winter an edict made Yue Grand Field Headquarters of the Southwest Circuit, commanding Minister of State Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.
idiomatic: In winter an edict made Yue grand field headquarters of the southwest circuit, commanding minister of state Pan Xiangyue and others to rescue Jiangling.

literal: In the first month of the sixth year the army halted at Yiyang; Jing Province had fallen; they then raided south as far as Ying Province, captured Liang Governor Wang Situ Lu Fahé, and took Ying Province.
idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year the army halted at Yiyang; Jing Province had fallen; they raided south to Ying Province, captured Liang governor and minister of state Lu Fahé, and took Ying.

literal: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched Honorary Equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.
idiomatic: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched honorary equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.

literal: When the court learned Jiangling had fallen, an edict ordered Yue to withdraw.
idiomatic: When the court learned Jiangling had fallen, an edict ordered Yue to withdraw.

literal: Yue himself had merit at Hanshan, Changshe, and the campaigns through Sui and Lu; his martial name weighed ever heavier.
idiomatic: Yue himself had merit at Hanshan, Changshe, and the campaigns through Sui and Lu; his martial name weighed ever heavier.

literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant, especially fond of wine and women; singing girls and dancing women, cauldrons set and bells struck — none of the princes matched him.
idiomatic: Yet by nature he was extravagant, especially fond of wine and women; singing girls, dancing women, cauldrons set and bells struck — no prince matched him.

literal: At first Gao Guiyan was orphaned young; the High Ancestor ordered Yue to raise him. Yue thought him too young and treated him with very thin courtesy.
idiomatic: Gao Guiyan was orphaned young; Gao Huan ordered Yue to raise him. Yue thought him too young and treated him with very thin courtesy.

literal: Guiyan harbored resentment within but never spoke of it.
idiomatic: Guiyan nursed resentment within but never spoke of it.

literal: When Guiyan became Commander of the Army and was greatly favored, Yue thought he owed Yue a debt and relied on him all the more.
idiomatic: When Guiyan became commander of the army and was greatly favored, Yue thought he owed a debt and relied on him all the more.

literal: Guiyan secretly built up his faults.
idiomatic: Guiyan secretly built up his faults.

literal: Yue built a mansion south of the city; behind the audience hall he opened a lane.
idiomatic: Yue built a mansion south of the city; behind the audience hall he opened a lane.

literal: Guiyan memorialized the emperor: "Prince of Qinghe builds his mansion, presumptuously imitating the imperial palace, making an Eternal Lane — only the gate-towers are missing.
idiomatic: Guiyan memorialized the emperor: "Prince of Qinghe builds his mansion in imitation of the palace, with an Eternal Lane — only the gate-towers are missing.

literal: " The Manifest Ancestor heard and hated it; he gradually grew distant from Yue.
idiomatic: " Gao Yang heard and hated it; he gradually grew distant from Yue.

literal: It happened that the Manifest Ancestor summoned a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier summoned her to his house — through his elder sister.
idiomatic: It happened that Gao Yang summoned a woman of Ye named Xue into the palace; Yue had earlier summoned her to his house — through his elder sister.

literal: The emperor had Xue's elder sister suspended and sawn apart, reproaching Yue for violating commoners' daughters.
idiomatic: The emperor had Xue's elder sister suspended and sawn apart, reproaching Yue for violating commoners' daughters.

literal: Yue said: "Your servant originally meant to take her but found her frivolous and did not use her — it was not violation.
idiomatic: Yue said, "I originally meant to take her but found her frivolous and did not — it was not violation.

literal: " The emperor grew angrier still.
idiomatic: " The emperor grew angrier still.

literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he sent Gao Guiyan to Yue's house to rebuke him sharply.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he sent Gao Guiyan to Yue's house to rebuke him sharply.

literal: Yue, anxious and fearful, knew not what to do; within days he died — so contemporary talk widely held he had been given poisoned wine.
idiomatic: Yue, anxious and fearful, knew not what to do; within days he died — contemporary talk widely held he had been given poisoned wine.

literal: Court and countryside mourned him.
idiomatic: Court and countryside mourned him.

literal: He was forty-four.
idiomatic: He was forty-four.

literal: An edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral; posthumously he was made Bearer of the Staff, Military Governor of Seven Provinces, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Ding Province; the yellow battle-axe was granted, an imperial carriage for the coffin provided, and two thousand bolts of burial goods; posthumous name Zhaowu.
idiomatic: An edict ordered the grand master of ceremonies to oversee the funeral; posthumously he was made bearer of the staff, military governor of seven provinces, grand preceptor, grand tutor, and governor of Ding Province; the yellow battle-axe was granted, an imperial carriage for the coffin provided, and two thousand bolts of burial goods; posthumous name Zhaowu.

literal: At first Yue with the High Ancestor had ordered the realm; the household kept private troops and stored weapons; more than a thousand suits of armor were hoarded.
idiomatic: At first Yue with Gao Huan had ordered the realm; the household kept private troops and stored weapons; more than a thousand suits of armor were hoarded.

literal: At the end of the Heir Apparent's reign Yue, because all under Heaven was at peace, memorialized asking to turn them in.
idiomatic: At the end of Gao Cheng's reign Yue, because the realm was at peace, memorialized asking to turn them in.

literal: The Heir Apparent, honoring the weight of close kin, gave him his full trust and said: "Uncle is of our inner flesh; your charge is to guard the walls — the armor you hold is meant for the state's use; why doubt and turn it in?
idiomatic: Gao Cheng, honoring close kin, gave him his full trust and said, "Uncle is of our inner flesh; your charge is to guard the walls — the armor you hold is meant for the state; why doubt and turn it in?

literal: " In the era of Wenxuan he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again was firmly refused.
idiomatic: " In Gao Yang's reign he also repeatedly asked to turn them in, and again was firmly refused.

literal: When about to die he left a final memorial thanking grace and again asked to submit the superior armor to the armory; only when the burial was complete was surrender permitted.
idiomatic: When about to die he left a final memorial thanking grace and again asked to submit the superior armor to the armory; only when the burial was complete was surrender permitted.

literal: In the Huangjian era he was given paired sacrifice in the Heir Apparent's temple hall.
idiomatic: In the Huangjian era he was given paired sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.

literal: Later when Guiyan rebelled, the Shizu Emperor knew his earlier slander and said: "Prince of Qinghe was loyal and fierce, exerting himself for the royal house — yet Guiyan destroyed him and came between my flesh and bone.
idiomatic: Later when Guiyan rebelled, Gao Zhan knew his earlier slander and said, "Prince of Qinghe was loyal and fierce, exerting himself for the royal house — yet Guiyan destroyed him and came between my flesh and bone.

literal: " Guiyan's property was confiscated; a hundred mouths of good and low slaves were granted to Yue's household.
idiomatic: " Guiyan's property was confiscated; a hundred mouths of good and low slaves were granted to Yue's household.

literal: Later, remembering Yue's merit, he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor; the rest as before.
idiomatic: Later, remembering Yue's merit, he was again posthumously made grand preceptor and grand tutor; other honors unchanged.

literal: His son Mai inherited the succession.
idiomatic: His son Gao Mai succeeded him.

literal: Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was precocious from youth and loved by the Manifest Ancestor.
idiomatic: Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was precocious from youth and loved by Gao Yang.

literal: At seven he was sent to attend the crown prince.
idiomatic: At seven he was sent to attend the crown prince.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Qing Province; on the day of investiture the Manifest Ancestor admonished him: "Your uncle formerly governed Qing Province with lasting kindness to the people; therefore I send you to comfort those common folk. Use your heart well — do not fall from his renown.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Qing Province; on the day of investiture Gao Yang admonished him, "Your uncle formerly governed Qing with lasting kindness; therefore I send you to comfort those people. Use your heart well — do not fall from his renown.

literal: " Mai answered in tears: "Your servant, receiving favor in tender years, has been rashly promoted; though I exhaust my limited powers, I fear disgracing my predecessor's governance.
idiomatic: " Mai answered through tears, "I have been rashly promoted while still young; though I exhaust my limited powers, I fear disgracing my predecessor's governance.

literal: " The emperor said: "Since you can speak thus, I need not worry.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Since you can speak thus, I need not worry.
